{{Short description|Mathematical theorem}}
The '''Koukoulopoulos–Maynard theorem''', historically known as the '''Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture''', is a [[theorem]] in [[mathematics]], specifically [[Diophantine approximation#Khinchin's theorem and extensions|Diophantine approximation]]. It was proposed as a conjecture by [[Richard Duffin|R. J. Duffin]] and [[Albert Charles Schaeffer|A. C. Schaeffer]] in 1941<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Duffin | first1=R. J. | last2=Schaeffer | first2=A. C. | title=Khintchine's problem in metric diophantine approximation | jfm=67.0145.03 | zbl=0025.11002 | journal=Duke Math. J. | volume=8 | issue=2 | pages=243–255 | year=1941 | doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-41-00818-9 }}</ref> and [[mathematical proof|proven]] in 2019 by [[Dimitris Koukoulopoulos]] and [[James Maynard (mathematician)|James Maynard]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Koukoulopoulos|first1=Dimitris|last2=Maynard|first2=James|date=2020|title=On the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/10.4007/annals.2020.192.1.5|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=192|issue=1|pages=251–257|doi=10.4007/annals.2020.192.1.5|jstor=10.4007/annals.2020.192.1.5|arxiv=1907.04593|s2cid=195874052}}</ref>

It states that if <math>f : \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^+</math> is a [[real number|real]]-valued [[function (mathematics)|function]] taking on positive values, then for [[almost all]] <math>\alpha</math> (with respect to [[Lebesgue measure]]), the [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]]

: <math>\left| \alpha - \frac{p}{q} \right| < \frac{f(q)}{q}</math>

has infinitely many solutions in [[coprime integers]] <math>p,q</math> with <math>q > 0</math> [[if and only if]]

: <math>\sum_{q=1}^\infty \varphi(q) \frac{f(q)}{q} = \infty,</math>

where <math>\varphi(q)</math> is [[Euler's totient function]].

A higher-dimensional analogue of this conjecture was resolved by Vaughan and Pollington in 1990.<ref name="Mon204">{{cite book | last=Montgomery | first=Hugh L. | author-link=Hugh Montgomery (mathematician) | title=Ten lectures on the interface between analytic number theory and harmonic analysis | series=Regional Conference Series in Mathematics | volume=84 | location=Providence, RI | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | year=1994 | isbn=978-0-8218-0737-8 | zbl=0814.11001 | page=204 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pollington |first1=A.D. |last2=Vaughan |first2=R.C. |author2-link=Bob Vaughan |year=1990 |title=The ''k'' dimensional Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/JTNB_1989__1_1_81_0/ |journal=[[Mathematika]] |volume=37 |pages=190–200 |doi=10.1112/s0025579300012900 |issn=0025-5793 |s2cid=122789762 |zbl=0715.11036 |number=2|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Har0268">{{cite book | last=Harman | first=Glyn | author-link=Glyn Harman | chapter=One hundred years of normal numbers | editor1-last=Bennett | editor1-first=M. A. | editor2-last=Berndt | editor2-first=B.C. | editor2-link=Bruce C. Berndt | editor3-last=Boston | editor3-first=N. | editor3-link=Nigel Boston | editor4-last=Diamond | editor4-first=H.G. | editor5-last=Hildebrand | editor5-first=A.J. | editor6-last=Philipp | editor6-first=W. | title=Surveys in number theory: Papers from the millennial conference on number theory | location=Natick, MA | publisher=A K Peters | pages=57–74 | year=2002 | isbn=978-1-56881-162-8 | zbl=1062.11052}}</ref>

== Introduction ==
That existence of the [[rational number|rational]] approximations implies [[divergent series|divergence]] of the [[series (mathematics)|series]] follows from the [[Borel–Cantelli lemma]].<ref name=Har0268/> The [[converse implication]] is the crux of the conjecture.<ref name=Mon204/>

There have been many partial results of the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture established to date. [[Paul Erdős]] established in 1970 that the conjecture holds if there exists a constant <math>c > 0 </math> such that for every [[integer]] <math>n</math> we have either <math>f(n) = c/n</math> or <math>f(n) = 0</math>.<ref name=Mon204/><ref name=Har27>{{cite book | last=Harman | first=Glyn | title=Metric number theory | series=London Mathematical Society Monographs. New Series | volume=18 | location=Oxford | publisher=[[Clarendon Press]] | year=1998 | isbn=978-0-19-850083-4 | zbl=1081.11057 | page=27}}</ref> This was strengthened by Jeffrey Vaaler in 1978 to the case <math>f(n) = O(n^{-1})</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Vaaler |first=Jeffrey D. |title=On the metric theory of Diophantine approximation |journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics |volume=76 |issue=2 |year=1978 |pages=527–539 |doi=10.2140/pjm.1978.76.527 |url=https://msp.org/pjm/1978/76-2/pjm-v76-n2-p18-s.pdf}}</ref><ref name=Har28>{{cite book | last=Harman | first=Glyn | title=Metric number theory | series=London Mathematical Society Monographs. New Series | volume=18 | location=Oxford | publisher=[[Clarendon Press]] | year=1998 | isbn=978-0-19-850083-4 | zbl=1081.11057 | page=28}}</ref>

More recently, this was strengthened to the conjecture being true whenever there exists some <math>\varepsilon > 0 </math> such that the series
:<math>\sum_{n=1}^\infty \left(\frac{f(n)}{n}\right)^{1 + \varepsilon} \varphi(n) = \infty.</math>
This was done by Haynes, Pollington, and Velani.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Haynes |first1=A. |last2=Pollington |first2=A. |last3=Velani |first3=S. |title=The Duffin-Schaeffer Conjecture with extra divergence |journal=Mathematische Annalen |volume=353 |issue=2 |pages=259–273 |year=2012 |doi=10.1007/s00208-011-0677-2 |arxiv=0811.1234 |s2cid=119159986}}</ref>

In 2006, Beresnevich and Velani proved that a [[Hausdorff measure]] analogue of the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture is [[logically equivalent|equivalent]] to the original Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture, which is a priori weaker. This result was published in the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Beresnevich | first1=Victor | last2=Velani | first2=Sanju | title=A mass transference principle and the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture for Hausdorff measures | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series | volume=164 | number=3 | year=2006 | pages=971–992 | zbl=1148.11033 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2006.164.971| arxiv=math/0412141 | s2cid=14475449 }}</ref>
